tldr: At the constant retrospective law the given causal risk ratio is one for every prevalence, yet normalized case and control perturbations force honest-null interval length. The existing two-branch mixed floor uses \(\mathfrak a(\kappa)=\max\{(4s_h+d)^{-1},\kappa/(4s_g+d)\}\) and scale \(N^{-\beta(\kappa)}\), with \(\beta(\kappa)=2\mathfrak a(\kappa)(s_g+s_h)\), under four strict benchmark comparisons. Its original and additional witnesses give \(N^{-5/18}\) and \(N^{-1/3}\). At the critical elbow \(s_h=d/4\), the multiscale testing-envelope characterization and null-length floor extend to every fixed dimension not divisible by four: \(\mathfrak W\asymp t^{-1/2}(\log t)^{3/4}\), while the paired-plus-regular benchmark has order \(t^{-1/2}\). The exact \(d=1\) result is retained as a corollary. The proposed extension to dimensions divisible by four is false under the frozen integer H\"older norm: an arbitrary-prior upper certificate instead gives \(\mathfrak W\lesssim t^{-1/2}(1+\log t)^{1/4}\), with the regular lower side \(\mathfrak W\gtrsim t^{-1/2}\). Supplied prevalence and any independent registry preserve the lower obstruction. Tightness of the integer bracket, other rough regimes, matching honest-interval upper rates, optimal constants, and improvements from genuinely higher-order-dependent priors outside the matched regime remain unresolved. Positioning is an incremental causal specialization of established functional-testing theory, with conditional priority for the exact comparison.
